lead: your loft is other people's, and the question was never put to you — so at forty you went under the arrangement looking for the evening you agreed to it, and there is no evening.
sun: a favour has a bottom like anything else. you go down through the object itself — the chair, the cartons, the standing agreement about somebody's dog — and what turns up underneath is what the leaving was doing for the one who left it: a claim kept live, a return kept possible, a piece of their week held in your name. item by item, you are right about this.
moon: the space refills. what got in did not come through a door, so taking one arrangement apart teaches the next person nothing — there was nothing for you to withdraw. within a season a different set of somebody's belongings occupies where the last set was, arriving the same way, on the same assumption, from a man who has heard only that you are easy about it.
pull: you have the true reason each of those cartons came to you. having it does not shut the loft, because the loft was never opened. it was only used.
tension: people who leave things with you are not thinking about it, which is the whole mechanism, so being told what they were doing arrives as an accusation out of nowhere. you kept the chair for eleven years without a murmur and then produced a motive for it — that reads as bitterness held a long time rather than as something found. the ones who hear it stop leaving things, and from outside it looks like you driving people off.
cost: an arrangement nobody ever spoke about can be stated out loud, accurately, with the year it began and what it was for, by the one person carrying it. saying it ends the arrangement and does not end the carrying: a fortnight later somebody's mother's piano is in your hall, from a woman who has heard nothing about any of this.

lead: she tells you the thing she has told nobody, and it takes about a minute, and you are already under it — into why this year, why you, and what the telling was meant to do.
sun: a confidence arrives pre-explained. people hand over a cause along with the thing, because the version they can say out loud is the version they have made survivable, and the survivable version is what you go under. what was done, then the year it got decided, then the arrangement it was protecting — and you are there before the coffee has cooled, with somebody who came to be held.
moon: what comes in is heard exactly, including the quarter-second where the story got smoothed, and the smoothing is where the digging starts. nor does it switch off when the door closes. months after the conversation is finished on their side, the account is being worked at over your sink, corrected, taken lower, on a person who believes the matter was put down that night.
pull: she wanted it held. it was held, and opened, and handed back with the reason underneath it, and the reason was right. that is the part nobody forgives.
tension: the first telling goes well. you are the least shockable person available and nothing shows on your face, so it comes out whole. the second time, they arrive with the thing and leave having heard what the thing was actually for, which was not asked for and cannot be unheard. after that you get the ordinary version, warmly, from people who like you, call you deep, and route the real material to somebody softer.
cost: in one sitting, from you, a person gets the reason they have done the same thing for twenty years, with the year on it, and it holds. what they told you does not leave when they do. it goes on being worked at, so by the next meeting you know more about that evening than the one who lived it, and no occasion exists for saying so.

lead: somebody sold a car on a sentence you said in the middle of a job, four layers off the bottom, thinking out loud — which is the only way any of this gets done at all.
sun: the descent is not a quiet operation. it runs for weeks and it runs aloud: the wrong version said into the room to see what comes back at it, then the next wrong version, then the muttering at the bench. that is the method, and moving it inside your skull stops it working. the bottom turns up at layer six. layers one to five were all spoken at full volume.
moon: people time themselves on the noise. after a decade near you they can hear which stage a job is at, and they act on stage two, because stage two is loud and sure of itself and the room has never known you to be wrong at the end of one. the finding lands at stage six, into a group that moved four weeks ago, on the wrong layer.
pull: you are right at the bottom and audible the whole way down. the people around you live off what you say at the halfway mark, and the halfway mark is where you are wrongest.
tension: the quiet gets read as well. a week without a word out of you registers as an all-clear, and somebody renews a lease on it. no setting exists where the working can be done off-air, and going silent is itself a signal, so keeping a verdict back requires issuing a different one. it gets called a mood, and dates get chosen around it, and nobody has said out loud that this is what they are doing.
cost: the whole route is audible, so a fault misread by four competent people for years comes apart in the open with the reasoning there for anybody who wants to check it. the reasoning is equally available at every wrong stage, to people making decisions that week, and the bottom arrives to a room that acted a month ago on something you were saying only to hear how it sounded.

lead: the offer was genuine, dated, and made in your own words: come and be here as long as you need. what the man in the spare bed did not know is that this house takes people apart.
sun: shelter makes a person talkative and unhurried, which is the condition the digging wants and cannot produce by itself. a guest with a key and no end date will hand over the whole account of what went wrong by the second week — and you take it down through the account, to the year underneath it, at your own table, kindly, while he is eating, and you are correct.
moon: the room is real and unconditional, which makes it impossible to walk out of. the person being opened has nowhere else this month, was asked here by you, and owes you the week. so the true thing said at the table cannot be argued down, or paid back, or left behind, and he sits in the kindest house he has been in and hears the bottom of his own life.
pull: you gave him the room and you meant it. the room is where he found out the actual reason, from the one person that month he could not walk away from.
tension: nobody warns anybody. the ones who have stayed describe the house as safe, and they mean it — warm, unmanaged, hours of it, no score being kept. what they say afterwards is that they went in exhausted and came out knowing a thing about themselves they had been getting by without. a few are grateful. hardly any come a second time, and the invitations keep going out at the same rate.
cost: a person at the worst point of their life gets a bed, a fortnight of quiet, and the actual cause of what put them there, without having to ask for any part of it. the version of themselves they arrived holding does not survive the fortnight, and it was your invitation that brought them into the house where it went.
